texts.facts: The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.552/19 Police Station New Ashok Nagar, Delhi. 2. The accident in the present case took place on 13.11.2019. It is the case of the petitioner that at around 07:00 PM, he was going to Mangal Bazar Road, M.V. -III, Delhi via Kaundali roadside on foot and when he reached at Vidya Bal Bhawan Public School, MIX Housing M.V.-III, offending motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-6SAE-7624, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from the back side and without blowing any horn and applying safety measures, the Ratan Kumar Dass vs Vikram Bhati And Anr. on 26 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177589666/ 1 driver of the offending vehicle hit the petitioner from back side, due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Driver managed to flee away from the spot and petitioner was admitted in LBS Hospital wherein MLC was prepared. 3. On notice of the petition, the respondent no. 1 & 2 appeared with IO at the time of filing of DAR. The respondents no. 1 & 2 who are the driver and owner of the offending motorcycle were given several opportunities to file reply but the same was not availed and their right to file WS was closed on 01.06.2022. 4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 31.08.2022 : - (i) Whether the petitioner Mr. Ratan Kumar Das suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 13.11.2019 at about 7:00 pm in front of Vidya Bal Bhawan Public School, MIX Housing M.V.- III, within the jurisdiction of PS New Ashok Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL 6SAE-7624 (motorcycle) by respondent no.1Vikram Bhati ? (OPP) (ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP) (iii) Relief 5. In order to establish his claim, petitioner Ratan Kumar Das has examined himself as PW-1. The respondents have not led any evidence.
texts.arguments: (New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656). 11. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act. In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box. 16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases. It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
